dehydrated_text:
In economics class, you may have been taught that the point of capitalism is to accumulate more capital. However, the true goal is to focus the energies of the peasants. Because attention and focus make a society more energetic. Hence, if a society is wealthy, it makes people lazy and complacent. The way to resolve this issue is through constant engagement in wars and the boom-bust cycle you might have learned about.

In economics, the boom-bust cycle is not natural to capitalism but artificial. People in charge intentionally destroy economies and wealth to make peasants work harder. Are you following along? So, that's the strategy we've used over these past few centuries, leading us today as the wealthiest society ever yet also the most miserable, anxious, and indebted.

The landlord class, capitalists, have figured out three mechanisms to extract energy: first, giving an illusion of freedom in life; second, making money the focus of your entire existence; third, creating anxiety in society through constant wealth destruction. Think of Jack Ma— despite his immense wealth, he still wants more because money is abstract and never enough.

When people are pushed too hard, they eventually revolt. So, the solution is to move. The landlord class can relocate somewhere else when anxiety becomes overwhelming, leaving peasants to destroy each other while they rebuild society. This process rules the world today— transnational capital, where wealthy people have no loyalty to nation or place but only to their capital.

In concrete terms, secret societies allow transnational capital to function and move from place to place. These societies exist because the landlord class and peasants are fundamentally different. Secret societies and transnational capital are essentially the same force that rules the world today.
